beats.care: Fighting near the Gulf keeps oil above $100. That shows up in petrol prices here, and worries families with relatives in the Gulf.
beats.what: Three years after Hamas attacked Israel, Israeli strikes on Gaza continue despite a ceasefire, and the US still blockades Iran.
beats.why: Israel wants Hamas gone. Iran backs Hamas and its allies. The US and Israel fear Iran's nuclear programme.

cards.body: This week marked 3 years since Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023. A Gaza ceasefire began on 10 October 2025, but Israeli airstrikes continue and Israel says it controls over 60% of Gaza. The US is still blockading Iran's ports.
All of them, living and dead, had been returned by January 2026 under the ceasefire deal.
cards.caption: people taken hostage on 7 Oct 2023

cards.body: Iran backs groups that fight Israel: Hamas in Gaza, Hezbollah in Lebanon, the Houthis in Yemen. The US and Israel call Iran's nuclear programme a threat. In February 2026 they struck Iran, and the fight spread across the region.
cards.title: why is Iran even involved?

cards.body: Costlier oil hits fuel, travel and delivery prices, and weakens the rupee. Millions of Indians live and work in Gulf countries, so every escalation is a family worry for a lot of people here.
On 8 Oct, Trump said the US won't attack Iran before the 3 November US midterm elections, while talks go on. But he also said the US blockade of Iran's ports stays in full force.

a.body: There will be no Hamas rule in Gaza. Hamas must fully disarm before Israel fully pulls out.

b.body: Disarming is tied to political conditions, including a Palestinian state. Strikes during a ceasefire break the deal.

cards.note: Hundreds of thousands of people in Gaza still live in tents or temporary shelters.

cards.q: Why does fighting near the Strait of Hormuz matter to India?
cards.why: Tankers carrying oil from the Gulf pass through Hormuz. Trouble there means costlier oil for India.
